title: Focus throttle weekly playbook and KPI scratchpad
body:
Purpose: a light, iterative personal playbook to keep a small set of high-leverage outcomes moving week-to-week. This is intentionally granular (daily/weekly), meant to pair with OKR-level tracking elsewhere.

High-level North Star (Q1–Q2): Increase throughput on infra-facing improvements so product teams get predictable 99th p95 improvements without regressions in cost. Personal role: reduce friction for infra rollouts and free up 8+ hours/week for focused design work.

Objectives (short):
1) Ramp focused deep work time to 18h/week (from baseline ~10h).
   - Metric: weekly deep-work hours logged (calendar-blocked, no Slack).
   - Target by end of quarter: 18h/week sustained for 3 consecutive weeks.
2) Shipping velocity for infra fixes: move weekly deploys impacting infra from 3 -> 8.
   - Metric: infra-impacting PRs merged / week (shippable + deployed to staging).
   - Quality guardrail: <=1 post-merge incident per 20 deploys.
3) Knowledge transfer: create 5 short runbooks/BLUF docs for common rollbacks and quantization tuning.
   - Metric: runbooks published and linked in team wiki.

Weekly snapshot (rolling 4 weeks):
- 2026-02-15 — 2026-02-21: deep work 9h, infra PRs merged 2, runbooks published 0. Notes: context-switching heavy; calendar spill.
- 2026-02-22 — 2026-02-28: deep work 12h, infra PRs merged 4, runbooks 1. Experimented with morning 90-min blocks.
- 2026-03-01 — 2026-03-07: deep work 14h, infra PRs merged 3, runbooks 1. Observed lower interrupt between 9–11am.
- 2026-03-08 — 2026-03-14 (current week): deep work 16h so far, infra PRs merged 5, runbooks 0. Focused on one larger rollout.

Micro-experiments (active):
A. Morning compacting (2x 90-min blocks, no meetings 9–12): hypothesis = fewer context switches => +4h deep work/week. Measure = calendar-block adherence + subjective focus score. Status: running week 3, adherence ~75%.
B. PR batching window (batch reviews to 3x/day at 10:30, 15:00, 17:30): hypothesis = reduce pull-in for notifications; Measure = number of interruptions and median review time. Status: pilot, needs stricter guardrails.
C. One-week 'no-upstream' carveout for doc-writing before demo weeks (no new PR merges on Tue): hypothesis = higher quality runbooks. Status: planned next week.

Hypotheses and signals to watch:
- If deep-work hours >15 for 2 consecutive weeks and infra PRs >=4/week, then cadence is sustainable.
- If post-merge incidents spike >1/10, pause batching and tighten review checklist.

Retrospective notes (quick):
- Wins: mornings working uninterrupted produced measurable lift; merged a refactor that reduced local repro time for SRE by ~30%.
- Friction: recurring ad-hoc infra asks from product on fast timelines. Need queueing ritual.
- Personal: decision fatigue in afternoons — try quick 20-min walk or caffeine taper.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How to delegate routine rollback approvals without adding ceremony? (bring to 1:1 with manager 2026-03-10).
- Which 3 runbooks are highest ROI? My pick: quantization rollback, nightly-batch fallback, and cache-priming script. Need quick input from Rafi.

Action list (next 7 days):
- [ ] Publish first draft runbook: "quantization rollback — BLUF" (target: 2026-03-12) — assign reviewer @Rafi.
- [ ] Block 9–11am daily and mark 2x 90-min deep blocks on calendar (ongoing).
- [ ] Try PR batching strictly for 3 business days (2026-03-10 to 2026-03-12) and record interruptions.
- [ ] Triage ad-hoc product requests into a single Slack thread + daily 2pm triage window.

Meeting prep bullets (1:1 with manager):
- Status on deep-work: progress against 18h target and ask for protected focus time policy.
- Request to formalize a lightweight rollback-approval (email-based) to unblock runbook testing.
- Ask for 0.5 FTE for doc-orchestration (temp) to help produce 5 runbooks by quarter end.

Quick wins (30–90 min):
- Draft BLUF + steps for quantization rollback (30m).
- Add one example to the runbook repo that shows a rollback command sequence (45m).

Signals I log (so I can measure trends):
- daily_deep_minutes: string note in calendar (e.g., "90+45")
- pr_merge_count_week: integer recorded in weekly note
- post_merge_incidents_week: integer
- runbooks_published_total: integer

Formatting notes: keep this doc blunt and time-boxed. If something moves to stable/mature (runbook done, experiment ended), move the link into personal OKR board and clear it from this ephemeral playbook.

Raw scratch entries (timestamped quick notes):
- 2026-03-02 10:15: disrupted by paging for infra-job; blocked focus for 45m. TODO: escalate to on-call rotation changes.
- 2026-03-04 16:40: realized PR reviews are <30m when batched; still feels like cognitive load later.
- 2026-03-07 09:05: 90-min block produced 2.5 pages of doc draft.

Tags for migrating later: #runbooks #deepwork #batching #infra-velocity #personal-kpi

If I revisit this in 2 weeks: checklist to evaluate experiment success = (deep-work >= 15h/wk AND infra-prs >=4 AND post-merge incidents <=1/10). If true, escalate for team policy to adopt morning focus windows."
